confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Leh food and drink prices. Restaurant meal anchors rest on travel-blog and budget-site ranges, including Rs 150-250 per person at budget eateries, Rs 250-600 per person at mid-range places, and about $3.5 budget and $8 mid-range per person on TripBase. The coffee figure is weakly supported: I found only one reported latte price of about Rs 130 and no cappuccino price. The beer figure rests on a TripBase average of about $2.5 and one Lonely Planet listing of Rs 250 for a beer at one venue. Draught beer is uncommon in Leh, so I treated beer as a typical bottled restaurant serving. I found no cocktail or wine prices, so those two are set from the beer price using a typical ratio for tourist bars, with cocktails about 1.7x beer and wine about 1.5x beer. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for the July peak season. I did not search for or inspect any listings or booking pages. I converted rupees at an assumed rate of about Rs 90 per USD, which I did not look up. Leh prices swing widely by season and venue, and everything here is lower confidence.
comparable_city_reasoning: No close comparable city. The estimates sit between Indian hill-tourism towns such as Manali and Rishikesh and the higher cost of a remote high-altitude destination with a short peak season and costly logistics. They are above typical lowland Indian cities for drinks and accommodation. Restaurant meals sit near the Himalayan tourist-town norm.
